classification.difficultyReason: Multiply by the squared denominator, solve the resulting quadratic inequality, and exclude the original pole.

answer.short:
$5<x\le15$.

Multiply by $(x-5)^2$, solve the quadratic inequality, and exclude $x=5$.
answer.worked:
The original denominator requires $x\ne5$. Multiply by $(x-5)^2$, which is positive on this domain:
$$\begin{align*}2x(x-5)&\ge3(x-5)^2\\3(x-5)^2-2x(x-5)&\le0\\(x-5)[3(x-5)-2x]&\le0\\(x-5)(x-15)&\le0\\5&\le x\le15\end{align*}$$
Excluding $x=5$ gives $5<x\le15$.
